title: Requirements clarification for onboarding open-model variants and version pinning in Model Catalog
creator: Sofia Lopez
description: Clarify product requirements, scope boundaries, and acceptance criteria for onboarding new open models into the Redwood Model Catalog. This ticket focuses on: required metadata for catalog entries, a version-pinning model for customers, compatibility notes (runtime/tooling/tokenizer/quantization), and minimal validation gates that prevent serving incompatible variants. Outcome: a precise spec for engineering and QA to implement an onboarding pipeline + UI/metadata contract.
background: As we expand the catalog with community open models, we need to ensure new entries are discoverable, safe to serve across our runtime variants (hosted/dedicated/private), and that customers can pin specific model versions reliably. Past ad-hoc onboarding produced mismatched tokenizer/runtime pairs and unclear fallback behavior. PM wants a repeatable onboarding contract that reduces incidents and accelerates model addition.
scope: In-scope: catalog metadata schema updates, version pinning semantics and UI text, CI validation checks for tokenization and kv-cache compatibility, onboarding checklist, acceptance criteria and rollout plan for the first 8 open-model variants. Out-of-scope: full automation of artifact publishing to customer-managed private deployments, license negotiations, and retrofitting pre-2025 catalog entries.
out_of_scope: Automated license approval; on-prem deployment packaging for air-gapped customers; building new quantization tooling (only spec required); UI redesign unrelated to version/pinning surfaces.
requirements: A. Catalog metadata contract: every new model entry must include these required fields: model_id, version (semver or commit-hash), architecture_family, tokenizer_family, tokenizer_version, max_sequence_length, recommended_context_window, quantization_profiles (list), supported_kv_cache_layouts, required_runtime_min_version, license_spdx, upstream_source_url, checksum_sha256.

B. Version pinning behavior: support three identifier forms: stable alias (eg 'stable'/'recommended'), semver (eg '3.0.1'), and immutable artifact id (eg commit hash or storage-object-id). Pinning must resolve deterministically in API responses and in UI. When a pinned version is unavailable on a particular runtime, the platform must reject the route with clear error and optional fallback guidance.

C. Compatibility notes: catalog entry must surface compatibility booleans and free-text notes for: tokenizer compatibility (tokenizer mismatch risk), kv-cache layout compatibility, required custom kernels, minimum runtime build, and whether INT8/FP16 quantizations are validated.

D. Validation gates in onboarding pipeline: automated checks that must pass before entry is marked publishable: tokenizer round-trip check on canonical prompt set; basic generate smoke test (sanity completions <=50 tokens) on hosted runtime; kv-cache warm/run check for 2 sequence lengths; quantized inference smoke tests for recommended quantization profiles (if provided); license/attribution verification step (manual or automated).

E. UI/SDK contract: the Console model detail page and the Redwood API responses must include 'pinned_version' and 'compatibility_issues' fields; SDKs should expose an error code MODEL_INCOMPATIBLE with a human-readable compatibility note when attempting to route to an unavailable variant.

F. Rollback and fallback rules: when runtime rejects a pinned version for capacity or incompatibility reasons, the system should not auto-fallback to a different major version without explicit customer opt-in; for hosted customers we should offer a fallback suggestion and a single-click 'use compatible variant' option in Console (opt-in requires explicit acknowledgement).

G. Observability: onboarding pipeline must emit a structured onboarding_event with success/failure reasons. Catalog entries must include a 'validated_at' timestamp and 'validation_results' summary string for quick triage.
H. Documentation: a concise Owner-facing onboarding checklist (Confluence/Drive) and a Customer-facing migration note template to appear in Console when a model version is deprecated.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Schema change merged: data model accepts and validates all required fields. Test fixtures for at least 8 sample open-model variants present in ENG repo.
2) Onboarding CI: a pipeline that runs tokenizer round-trip and smoke generation; results recorded in 'validation_results'. All sample fixtures pass the CI in a dev environment.

3) Version pinning: API accepts calls referencing pinned_version by semver and artifact-id; for pinned artifact-id the resolution is immutable and included in API response. Unit tests cover alias->resolved mapping.

4) Compatibility surface: Console model detail shows compatibility booleans and a free-text compatibility note. Attempting to route via API to a runtime with incompatible variant returns MODEL_INCOMPATIBLE and the note.
5) No silent auto-fallback: system does not route to a different major version unless customer toggles opt-in in Console; integration test asserts opt-in behavior.
6) Security review: security_signoff document attached to catalog entry; any models with license issues flagged and blocked from publish.
7) Docs: onboarding checklist and customer migration template published and linked from Console; QA verifies links and templates.
8) Metrics: first-run onboarding pass rate for pilot models >= 85%; time to onboard (from PR -> publish) < 48 hours for models that pass automated checks.
9) Observability: onboarding_event emitted and visible in DevOps logging for each run; validation_results string available on model detail.
10) Edge case tests: tokenizer mismatch and kv-cache layout mismatch both produce deterministic error codes and human-readable notes.
11) Release gating: feature flagged and disabled by default for existing customers; enabled in dark-launch for internal pilot accounts.
12) Security flag set to true if model requires HSM KMS integration or contains sensitive training data classification.
success_metrics: Reduce catalog-related support tickets by 40% in 3 months after launch.
Onboarding throughput: ability to validate and publish 10 open models per week in pilot cadence.
Metadata completeness: >=95% of catalog entries have all required fields populated within 24 hours of publish.
First-pass CI success rate for new models >=85%.
Mean time from onboarding PR to publish <48 hours for validated models.
No customer incidents from incompatible tokenizer/runtime mismatches in first 90 days.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal pilot): implement schema + CI for 3 curated open models (Llama-3-base, Mistral-Instruct-small, Falcon-7B-mini) and run onboarding pipeline in dev infra. (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (dark launch): enable read-only catalog page + Console detail for internal pilot accounts and the SRE team; allow adding entries behind feature flag. (1 week)
Phase 2 (limited beta): open onboarding to a set of partners and 10 early adopters; require security review for publish. Monitor metrics and support tickets. (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (general availability): enable for all hosted customers and provide migration templates; announce in release notes. (after signoff)
Rollback guard: feature flag controlled; rollback steps documented in Confluence; emergency disable route in Console for immediate unpublish.
Pilot exit criteria: sample model set passes acceptance criteria 1-11; security signoff obtained; <5 critical issues in beta.
open_questions: Q1: Who owns manual license verification and what is the expected SLA for manual steps?
Q2: For private deployments, do we require customers to sync model artifacts themselves or allow Redwood to push validated artifacts? (policy + legal question)
Q3: Do we allow an alias 'recommended' to automatically rotate to a newer patch version? If so, how do we signal breaking changes to customers?
Q4: What telemetry level is acceptable for tokenization failures (PII exposure risk)?
Q5: Are there additional runtime constraints (GPU memory/special kernels) that must be surfaced as hard blockers vs. advisory notes?
Q6: Which engineering team will own the onboarding CI and the corresponding maintenance backlog (serving runtime infra or model team)?
notes: Engineering to propose minimal schema migration plan (backfill strategy for existing entries) and a thin adapter in the SDK to surface pinned_version. Security to run a tabletop review for license/attribution policy. Design to provide Console copy for fallback flow. PM will coordinate pilot model list and partner invites.
